<!-- pr-reviewer: ff961c295b7f0071a2e5239b448e513cd66d81b1 -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** Reviewed at the effort:high tier (gouge law, safety floor).

## What looks good
- Strictly additive to the verdict. Before, `Trace::of` returned `None` for G18/G19 arcs and the wall reading was skipped; now `walled` is only ever an extra `||` beside the unchanged `gouged` (section.rs:114-117). No gouge flagged on main can stop being flagged. The only risk is a false refusal, and that is bounded (below).
- Read-never-farther-than-truth holds by construction. Planar: the exact segment, with an interior turn read at `c +- r_hi` (`ARC_PAD` past the larger endpoint radius), so it can only be longer than the cut. Helical: a polyline read against `floor + r d^2/8 + band width`. That is the standard interpolation bound, and the normal coordinate is linear in the sweep so it adds nothing. The unit test checks this against 20k-point dense sampling for both planes, both directions, and arcs over and under a half turn.
- Fail-closed paths are right: a non-finite centre or coordinate gives `Trace::Unread`, which is a gouge. Degenerate radius or sweep reads as the straight move, as `cl::arc_chords` cuts it. Loops are bounded by `MAX_ARC_CHORDS`; the 1e9 helix is pinned. No `unwrap`, `expect`, `panic!` or unchecked indexing outside tests. The `want as usize` cast is guarded by `is_finite() && >= 1.0` and `.min(MAX_ARC_CHORDS)`.
- Pinning tests are real: the end-to-end pin asserts the joints read the vertex clear and the verdict is `Gouge` (shown failing without the fix), with a clean twin for false refusals.
- Relation to #905: that issue is closed and its fix (#942) is merged. This PR is the G18/G19 follow-up (#946) that was split out during #942's review, and it builds directly on vilts's `arc_wall.rs`. It keeps `Trace::Arc` and `XyArc` semantics, and the `Vec` -> fixed-buffer change in `dist_seg` is the #942 review note. The tests moved from `app/tests` to `sim/tests` unchanged apart from the path, and the 3 `boundary_arc_walls` tests still pass. It touches nothing vilts has open that I could find, but vilts should get a courtesy ping that their module gained a variant.
- Housekeeping: provenance line, decision file `docs/decisions/946-...md` (not `RECOMMENDED.md`), no CHANGELOG edit, no snapshot PNGs, no process files, no new deps, no `build.rs`. Body has a `Changelog:` line and ends `Fixes #946`. File sizes are fine (new module 221 lines).

## Local results (merged with main; "Already up to date", so head == merge)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-sim` (all binaries, incl. `boundary_arc_planes` 3, `boundary_arc_walls` 3, lib `verify::` 14) | all ok, 0 failed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app` `--test verify_arc_reading` (6), `wall_arc_entry` (7), `vertical_arc_entry` (3), `solid_law` (4), `corner_blend` (5), `plasma_gate` (6) | all ok |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

## Requested before merge
None.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. False-refusal reach: `wall_gouge` ignores Z for straight moves already, so a G18/G19 lead-in or lead-out arc that stands above the stock top near a wall is now read the same way. That matches the straight-move behaviour, so it is consistent, but it is the one place a new refusal could show up in a real program. No generator emits helical XZ/YZ arcs today (per the body), and the existing arc-entry suites are green.
2. In the no-model case `Trace::Poly::crosses` is the plain polyline crossing test, approximate at the pad scale (~0.1 um), as the body says. It can only decide which branch is taken, not remove a gouge.
3. #946 is labelled P0 and in-review; GitHub will close it on merge.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: b53d75a4408bd41ab441d3dac8a7d28dd0a09516 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** This is an independent high-tier review (gouge law, safety floor) at head `b53d75a`. The head already contains current `main` (3e9b8ae1, with #911), so the trial merge was a no-op and the tree builds as is.

### What looks good
- **Geometry is right.** XZ uses `(u, v, w) = (z, x, y)`, so X = `cv + r sin` and its extremes are at +/- pi/2. YZ uses `(y, z, x)`, so Y = `cu + r cos` and its extremes are at 0 / pi. `in_sweep` is measured from the ccw start. That means a planar arc is read as the exact segment between its X (or Y) extremes. This includes an arc over a half turn that doubles back: its footprint is still the [min, max] segment, and the unit test's `(-1.0, 3.5)` sweep covers that case. Interior extremes are read at `r_hi`, which is conservative.
- **The helical bound is sound.** The normal coordinate is linear in the sweep, so the only interpolation error is in-plane, `r d^2 / 8`, plus the radius band. The polyline is read at `floor + pad`, so it never reads farther than the truth. A huge radius hits `MAX_ARC_CHORDS` and the pad grows: that refuses more, it never misses. The `want as usize` cast is guarded and saturating, a NaN fails closed (`Unread`), and there is no unwrap or panic outside tests.
- **It only adds readings.** The joint union and #942's XY-arc reading are untouched (`Trace::Arc` and `Seg` are the same code). The new reading is the continuous limit of the joint points, compared against the same edges and the same `floor`, so it cannot drop a conviction main gives.
- The test move to `crates/sim/tests` follows #921. The fixed buffer replaces the per-edge `Vec`. There is a decision file and a provenance line, and every file is under 400 lines. No golden moved.

### Local results (head = merged with main)
| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-sim --tests` (all 56 binaries, incl. `boundary_arc_planes` 3, `boundary_arc_walls` 4, lib 73) | 445 passed, 0 failed |
| app `verify_arc_reading` / `wall_arc_entry` / `solid_law` / `solid_law_goldens` / `shoulder_adaptive` / `golden_cl` / `conformance` / `vertical_arc_entry` | 7 / 7 / 4 / 1 / 3 / 25 / 6 / 3, all pass |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

(`boundary_arc_walls` now lives in sim, so it ran in the sim row.)

**Scratch probes (local only, deleted, never committed).** Fixture: the PR's own r 200 arc, with the vertex at the spot hidden between joints. Each case ran for G18 and G19, CW and CCW, on both sides of the footprint:
- Floor 3.99: d 3.989 gives `Gouge` and d 3.991 is clean in every case. The floor is exact in both directions.
- #911 with `model_excess` 0.008 (tightened floor 3.998): d 3.995 gives `Gouge`. The wall reading uses the same tightened `floor` as the joints (`section.rs:104/119`).
- With a model, the same corner on a block whose top is below the arc is clean, and the corner beside the arc gives `Gouge`.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (non-blocking)
1. **Z is not read, by design inherited from main.** The wall reading compares the whole XY footprint against the walls with no Z. With a model, walls come from the section at the move's lowest endpoint, so a wall below the cutter is not a wall: my "block below" probe was clean. That is correct for built paths, because `PathBuilder::push_arc_in` splits vertical arcs at Z extrema (they are Z-monotone).
   Without a model, every region edge is a wall at any Z. So a G18 arc entirely above the stock top, passing a region vertex 3.9 mm off, is now convicted where its joints were clear. Main's straight-move reading (#43) already convicts the same footprint as a G1 above the top (my probe: `Gouge` for both). The new reading is no stricter than the straight-move law. Any false refusal is on the safe side, not a missed gouge. If Boundary mode ever wants the Area-mode `wall_top` trim, it applies to straight moves and both arc kinds together.
2. A full-circle XZ / YZ arc (`from == to`) has zero sweep under `rem_euclid` and reads as the zero-length move. That matches `cl::arc_chords` and `sweep()` across the codebase (the builder refuses it), so this PR adds no new gap. Noted only.
3. A non-Z-monotone vertical arc built outside `PathBuilder` would get its section at the endpoints' lowest Z, not at the arc's own lowest point. This was already true of the joint reading, and the solid law (b2) samples it.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
